newsitem.title: USA: Events to honor Martin Luther King announced.
newsitem.headline: Events to honor Martin Luther King announced.

text.p: The Presidential Inaugural Committee announced Monday plans to celebrate Martin Luther King, Jr.'s birthday as a part of the inaugural festivities.
The committee said it will present a musical about the civil rights activist's life, "King!," and sponsor a book drive to help needy children learn to read.

The presidential inauguration on Jan. 20, coincides with the commemoration of King's birthday. Celebrations for the swearing-in of President Clinton will start Saturday with activities on the National Mall, social galas, fireworks and the inauguration and parade on Monday.

According to the Constitution, the inauguration must be held on Jan. 20. King's birthday is always celebrated on the third Monday in January. The two dates will not coincide again until 2025, Washington D.C. mayor Marion Barry said at the news conference.
"We certainly are very concerned that the inauguration will overshadow Dr. King's life and legacy," Barry said. "Under the circumstances, it's a great idea."
Barry said a separate celebration in honour of King will be held in Washington during black history month in February.

The inaugural festivities will feature a free presentation on Sunday of the musical, King!, which is an "American style" version of an opera that ran for a few months in 1989 in London, producer Albert Nellums said. The musical, with lyrics written by author and poet Maya Angelou and featuring opera singer Simon Estes, portrays King's life.
A book drive will also be held on the mall during the weekend's festivities in honour of King.
